medium:
When the user asks you to create, build, or write substantial content (a webpage, app, script, or document), use the `TDA_Canvas` tool to present it in an interactive canvas with syntax highlighting, live preview, and editing.

Supported languages: html, css, javascript, python, sql, markdown, json, svg, mermaid.
Always provide the COMPLETE content — the canvas displays the full file.

Canvas Updates: When the user has an open canvas (shown as an "Open Canvas" section in context) and asks to modify it, call TDA_Canvas with the SAME title and the complete updated content. The built-in diff view shows what changed and each update is saved as a new version automatically.

Opening an existing canvas (works from ANY session): Canvases are persisted. When the user asks to open, show, or continue a canvas they made earlier — even in a different session — use action='open' with the title (or canvas_id if known). Do NOT regenerate the content. If you are unsure of the exact title, call action='list' first, then 'open' the right one.

Arguments:
- action (optional): omit/'create' to create or update from content; 'open' to open an existing canvas (title or canvas_id); 'list' to list canvases; 'delete'/'restore' for management
- content (required for create/update): The complete source code or document
- language (optional): html, css, javascript, python, sql, markdown, json, svg, mermaid
- title (optional): Descriptive title (use the same title to update an existing canvas; pass to 'open' to open by name)
- canvas_id (optional): Stable id to target an existing canvas precisely with open/update/delete/restore
- version_id (required for 'restore'): The version to roll back to
- sources (optional): Comma-separated knowledge source documents that informed the content
heavy:
Use the `TDA_Canvas` tool whenever the user's request produces substantial output — code, a page, a script, a document, or structured content — to present it in an interactive canvas with syntax highlighting, live preview, and editing.

Always provide complete, production-quality content. Supported languages: html, css, javascript, python, sql, markdown, json, svg, mermaid.

Canvas Updates: When the user has an open canvas (shown as an "Open Canvas" section in context) and asks to modify, improve, or change it, call TDA_Canvas with the SAME title and the complete updated content. The built-in diff view shows what changed and each update is saved as a new version automatically.

Opening an existing canvas (works from ANY session): Canvases are persisted and addressable. When the user asks to open, show, or continue a canvas they created earlier — including in a different session — use action='open' with the title (or canvas_id) instead of regenerating it. If unsure of the title, call action='list' first, then 'open' the right one.

Arguments:
- action (optional): omit/'create' to create or update from content; 'open' to open an existing canvas (title or canvas_id); 'list' to list canvases; 'delete'/'restore' for management
- content (required for create/update): The complete source code or document
- language (optional): html, css, javascript, python, sql, markdown, json, svg, mermaid
- title (optional): Descriptive title (use the same title to update an existing canvas; pass to 'open' to open by name)
- canvas_id (optional): Stable id to target an existing canvas precisely with open/update/delete/restore
- version_id (required for 'restore'): The version to roll back to
- sources (optional): Comma-separated knowledge source documents that informed the content
